finite_candidate_design_catalog.reason: It measures the order-invariant marginal diversity of scale-free own-bar close locations. Existing close-location definitions measure a directional first moment or adjacent serial persistence, while the existing close occupancy entropy normalizes prices by the whole-session price range rather than by each bar's auction interval.
The ten equal-width bins and normalized Shannon operator are imported unchanged from the terminal fixed-bin occupancy definition; no bin-count or entropy-estimator search is allowed.

selected_candidate.name: intraday_own_bar_close_location_entropy_10b_240m
selected_candidate.economic_hypothesis: A broad distribution of minute closes across their own auction ranges indicates two-sided price acceptance and resilient local liquidity rather than systematic pinning to one boundary, and that auction resilience may persist from the next open through the third close.
selected_candidate.formula: For every positive-range selected bar compute x=(log(close)-log(low))/(log(high)-log(low)) in [0,1]. Map x to one of ten fixed equal-width bins floor(10*x), with exact x=1 assigned to bin 9. Pool all informative bars, require at least 120, compute p_k=count_k/n, and return -sum_{p_k>0}(p_k*log(p_k))/log(10).
selected_candidate.source_grid: Require the raw 09:30 row for immutable source identity; use exactly 09:31-11:30 and 13:01-15:00 and exclude 09:30.
selected_candidate.support: Require every selected high, low, and close to be finite and strictly positive with low<=close<=high. A high=low bar is noninformative and contributes no bin count. Require at least 120 positive-range bars; never impute, bridge, weight, or replace a state.
selected_candidate.floating_point_rule: Use float64 natural-log distances. Canonicalize only values within 1e-12 of 0 or 1 to the exact endpoint; any other state outside [0,1] is invalid.
selected_candidate.valid_range: [0,1] under normalized natural-log Shannon entropy with no clipping other than the stated endpoint canonicalization
